documents.title: Why the city's bike-share scheme is losing money
documents.text:
Two years after its much-publicized launch, the Corvin bike-share scheme is struggling to cover its costs. The system, which offers 1,200 bicycles at 140 docking stations, was meant to become self-financing by the end of its second year. Instead, it posted a loss of 1.9 million dollars, and the city council, which guarantees any deficit, is now asking whether the project should continue in its present form.

Ridership has been healthy. The bikes are used about four times a day on average, a figure that compares favorably with similar schemes elsewhere. The problem lies in what happens between rides. Staff must collect bicycles from the outer districts, where few people want to return them, and redistribute them to the center; this accounts for nearly half of the operating budget. Vandalism and theft add a further burden, with roughly one bike in ten needing repair each month.

Operator Cleo Vasquez insists that the scheme remains a good investment. She notes that the system has taken an estimated 3,000 car journeys off the roads each week. Her proposal is to introduce small penalties for leaving bikes outside designated zones and to offer discounts to users who return them to busy stations. Opposition councillor Ian Marsh is less convinced. "The principle is sound, but the numbers do not add up," he says. "We need a clear plan, not more promises."

choices: The growing popularity of cycling among older adults
The money troubles of a public transport project
A decision to ban all cars from the city center
The theft of equipment from several docking stations
questions.explanation: The bike-share scheme is losing money and the council is reconsidering it.

questions.prompt: What is the largest cost for the scheme?
choices: Paying for the docking stations in the center
Repairing damage caused by careless users
Advertising the service to all residents
Moving bicycles from one district to another
questions.explanation: Collecting and redistributing bicycles accounts for nearly half of the operating budget.

questions.prompt: What does Ms. Vasquez suggest doing?
choices: Rewarding users who help to balance the system
Reducing the number of stations in the center
Closing the scheme in the outer districts
Raising the price of every ride by half
questions.explanation: She proposes discounts for returning bikes to busy stations and small penalties for leaving them outside zones.

questions.prompt: What is Mr. Marsh's opinion?
choices: He wants the scheme to be closed immediately
He believes the bikes are used too rarely
He doubts that the figures support the project
He supports the operator's proposals fully
questions.explanation: He says the principle is sound but the numbers do not add up and asks for a clear plan.

documents.title: Staff parking: temporary arrangements
documents.text:
To: All staff, Linden Park campus
From: Gareth Ellis, Site Services
Date: 9 February

Between 23 February and 15 May, the main staff car park will be resurfaced in three phases. During each phase, one third of the spaces will be unavailable. Phase 1 (23 February to 20 March) affects the northern section, Phase 2 (23 March to 17 April) the central section, and Phase 3 (20 April to 15 May) the southern section. Signs will show which areas are open on each day.

To limit congestion, we ask staff to consider alternatives. A free shuttle will run from the Fairview Road overflow lot every ten minutes between 7:30 and 9:30 a.m. and between 4:30 and 6:30 p.m. Staff who choose to cycle may use the secure cage near Building C, and anyone who commits to using public transport for the full period will receive a 20 dollar reimbursement toward their monthly pass, up to a maximum of 60 dollars. Applications must be submitted before 20 February.

Please note that visitor spaces will not be affected, and staff must not park in them. Vehicles left in closed areas will be towed at the owner's expense. Employees with disabilities who require a designated space should contact me directly, and arrangements will be made close to the main entrance throughout the works.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the memo?
choices: To warn employees about a rise in parking fees now
To ask for volunteers for a building project
To explain how staff can cope while work is done
To announce a new bus route to the campus
questions.explanation: The memo describes the resurfacing work and offers alternatives for getting to work.

questions.prompt: Which part of the car park will be closed in April?
choices: The central section first, then the southern one
The northern section for the whole of the month
Only the section located near the visitor spaces
All three sections of the car park at once
questions.explanation: Phase 2 (central) ends on 17 April and Phase 3 (southern) starts on 20 April.

questions.prompt: How much could a staff member receive for using public transport?
choices: 20 dollars for every week of the trial
A complete monthly pass paid in full
100 dollars for the whole period
No more than 60 dollars in total
questions.explanation: The reimbursement is 20 dollars toward the monthly pass, up to a maximum of 60 dollars.

questions.prompt: What will happen to a car left in a closed area?
choices: It will be moved to the visitor spaces
It will be removed at the owner's cost
The owner will receive a written warning
It will be parked in the overflow lot
questions.explanation: Vehicles left in closed areas will be towed at the owner's expense.

documents.title: Tech support chat with an internet provider
documents.text:
Customer (Omar Haidari): Hi, my internet has been dropping several times a day for the past week. I work from home and it's affecting my video calls.
Agent (Tess): I'm sorry to hear that, Mr. Haidari. Can you tell me which router you use and how long you've had the service?
Customer: It's the Nexa 300 supplied by you, and I've had the contract for about three years.
Agent (Tess): Thank you. I can see some instability on your line in our system. The connection speed is falling during the evening hours, which suggests congestion in your neighborhood rather than a fault in your home.
Customer: But I'm having the problem in the morning as well.
Agent (Tess): That's useful to know. In that case, it may be a problem with the router. It's quite old, and we've seen similar reports. I can send you a new model for free; it should arrive in three working days.
Customer: Three days is a long time. Is there any way to get something sooner?
Agent (Tess): I can book a technician for tomorrow between 8 and 12, but there'd be a charge of 45 dollars unless the problem turns out to be on our side. Would you like me to do that?
Customer: I'll wait for the router. If it doesn't fix it, I'll call again.

questions.prompt: What problem does Mr. Haidari report?
choices: His bill has increased without notice
His connection keeps being interrupted
His router will not turn on at all
His videos play with no sound
questions.explanation: His internet has been dropping several times a day.

questions.prompt: Why does Tess change her opinion about the cause?
choices: The connection speed is higher during the evening
The router had been replaced only a short time ago
Other customers in his area have made no complaints
Problems also happen when few people are online
questions.explanation: She first suspects congestion in the evening, but he says problems happen in the morning too, so the router becomes the likely cause.

questions.prompt: What is a disadvantage of the free router?
choices: It will not arrive immediately
It costs 45 dollars to install
It works only in the morning
It requires a new contract
questions.explanation: It should arrive in three working days, which he considers a long time.

questions.prompt: What does Mr. Haidari decide?
choices: To change to a different internet provider soon
To cancel his contract before the end of the week
To test the new router before calling again
To pay for a technician to visit him tomorrow
questions.explanation: He will wait for the router and call again if it doesn't fix the problem.

documents.title: Reference letter from a former landlord
documents.text:
To whom it may concern,

I am pleased to write in support of Elena Kowalczyk, who rented a two-bedroom apartment from me at 22 Poplar Street from March 2019 until last month. In that time, she was an exemplary tenant. The rent was paid on the first of every month without a single exception, and the apartment was returned in better condition than it was found, since she repainted the living room at her own initiative and repaired a loose cabinet in the kitchen.

Ms. Kowalczyk also proved to be a considerate neighbor. When a water pipe burst on the floor above hers during the winter of 2021, she contacted the other residents and the emergency plumber, which prevented considerable damage to the building. I received no complaints about noise during her tenancy, which is unusual in a building with many young families.

She is leaving only because her employer has relocated her to another city. I would not hesitate to rent to her again, and I am confident that she will take the same care of any property in her charge. If you require further information, please do not hesitate to contact me by telephone.

Sincerely,
Walter Brandt

choices: To announce the sale of an apartment in the building
To request a payment owed by a former neighbor
To assist a former tenant in finding a new home
To report a problem with a pipe in the building
questions.explanation: The landlord recommends Ms. Kowalczyk as a tenant to whom it may concern.

questions.prompt: What did Ms. Kowalczyk do that went beyond her obligations?
choices: She improved the apartment before she left
She paid the rent a month in advance
She bought furniture for the kitchen
She found a new tenant for the apartment
questions.explanation: She repainted the living room and repaired a loose cabinet on her own initiative.

questions.prompt: What is suggested about the building?
choices: It was built recently in 2019
It has had frequent noise complaints
It is owned by Ms. Kowalczyk's employer
Many of its residents have small children
questions.explanation: The landlord says the lack of noise complaints is unusual in a building with many young families.

questions.prompt: The word "exemplary" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to
choices: typical
model
demanding
inexperienced
questions.explanation: A tenant who always pays on time and improves the apartment is a 'model' tenant.

documents.title: Fenwick Science Museum: Group visits
documents.text: Schools and community groups of ten or more may book a guided visit at least three weeks in advance. Visits last 90 minutes and are led by an educator. Admission for groups is 6 dollars per student and 9 dollars per adult, and one adult is admitted free for every ten students. The planetarium show costs an additional 3 dollars per person and must be requested when booking. Lunch can be eaten in the picnic room, which holds sixty people, but must be reserved. Groups arriving by coach can use the drop-off bay on Mill Road; the coach must then park at the Eastgate car park.

documents.title: Booking request: Year 8 visit
documents.text:
Dear Fenwick Museum,

I teach science at Hollins Secondary School and I would like to bring forty-eight Year 8 students on Wednesday 12 November, with five accompanying adults. We would like to see the planetarium show, and we need a place to eat lunch. I am also wondering whether you have worksheets that link to our curriculum on energy. One of our students uses a wheelchair, so please let me know about access.

Many thanks,
Fiona Gallagher

documents.title: Re: Booking request: Year 8 visit
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Gallagher,

Wednesday 12 November is available at 10:30. I have reserved the picnic room for 12:15 to 1:15. Every gallery is accessible by lift, and a wheelchair user will find the planetarium easy to enter. Our energy-themed worksheets can be downloaded from the schools page, and the educator will adapt the tour accordingly.

Please note that a booking requires a deposit of 100 dollars, to be paid within a week, and that the planetarium show begins at 12:00, so we suggest eating after it. I have also noted that you need to book three weeks in advance; as the date is nineteen days away, I have made an exception on this occasion.

Regards,
Ahmed Farouk, Education Officer

questions.prompt: What is Ms. Gallagher's purpose in writing?
choices: To apply for a job as an educator
To arrange a trip for her class to a museum
To complain about the museum's prices
To ask for materials on energy for the library
questions.explanation: She wants to book a visit for students and asks about the show, lunch, resources and access.

questions.prompt: What exception does the museum make?
choices: It lets the adults enter without paying anything
It allows the coach to park right next to the entrance
It provides lunch for the whole group at no cost
It takes a booking made less than three weeks ahead
questions.explanation: The date is nineteen days away, less than the three weeks required.

questions.prompt: How much will the group pay for admission, without the show?
choices: 297 dollars
288 dollars
342 dollars
333 dollars
questions.explanation: Students: 48 x 6 = 288. With 48 students, four adults enter free, so only one of the five adults pays 9 dollars. Total 297 dollars.

questions.prompt: What does Mr. Farouk recommend about lunch?
choices: To eat before arriving at the museum
To eat on the coach in the parking lot
To eat after the planetarium show
To bring lunch only for the adults
questions.explanation: The planetarium show starts at 12:00, so they suggest eating afterward, in the picnic room at 12:15.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in Mr. Farouk's reply?
choices: Access for a wheelchair user
A deposit needed to confirm the booking
The cost of the planetarium show
The time at which the visit begins
questions.explanation: He mentions access, the deposit and the start time, but not the price of the show; that comes from the web page.
